title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Stocks reversed an AI-jitters selloff to close higher Thursday (Dow +1.1%, S&P 500 +0.3%, Nasdaq +0.1%) after the S&P's longest calm streak since 2020 broke earlier in the week on AI-bubble fears.

Markets: Treasury yields fell sharply as investors sought safety — the 10-year dropped to 5.09%, its biggest one-day drop since August 2025 — while gold rose ~1.5-2% and crude climbed ~2.7% to ~$97/bbl.

Markets: Hot September PPI (+6.3% y/y, a 4+ year high) on top of 3.7% CPI is strengthening the case for the Fed to hike at its meeting in two weeks; industrial production data and several bank earnings (Travelers, Citizens Financial, Truist) are due Friday.

Companies: Anthropic told investors it was cash-flow positive in Q3 with revenue up ~50% q/q to $16.8B, offering Wall Street evidence AI can be a sustainable business amid bubble fears ahead of a potential IPO some see valued near $2T.
Companies: CoreWeave swung wildly — down more than 15% Wednesday and further Thursday morning on rate fears — before rallying to close +5.9% after Nvidia's Jensen Huang voiced support.
Macro/Policy: The FTC subpoenaed OpenAI and Anthropic for documents on AI safety incidents as part of a consumer-protection probe, and plans to compel executives to testify.
Macro/Policy: Nvidia's Huang said he'd cut off chip supply to any customer building "unsafe" AI, while Bill Gates is ramping up his own AI-safety advocacy push, personally lobbying CEOs.
